At Red Barn, we believe wealth is more than numbers — it’s the values you carry forward. Our team delivers risk-managed, tax-aware portfolios and family-first planning that provide peace of mind today and legacy clarity tomorrow.

[ABOUT US](/about)

## The Red Barn Difference

#### **Institutional strategies, no gatekeeping** 

* * *

We bring “pension-style” diversification—once reserved for the ultra-wealthy—into family portfolios, without watering it down. 

#### **Calibrated for today’s markets**

* * *

Risk-managed, tax-aware portfolios designed for volatile markets and long horizons. 

#### **Beyond retirement income**

* * *

Peace of mind today; legacy clarity tomorrow. Wealth isn’t just what you build—it’s what you carry forward.

#### **Aligned & accountable**

* * *

Discretionary management focused on your plan, your liabilities, and the people you love. 

#### Book an intro call

Take 15 minutes to meet your team and share your financial goals

[Book](/start-here)

![Group of smiling people gathered outdoors, with a pregnant woman at the center, surrounded by family members and friends, during sunset in a park with trees.](/images/b4d98aea84-jennifer-kalenberg-FEWg2B2o2wY-unsplash.webp)

## The Family Meeting 

#### Most families plan how assets will move—few plan how values will. The Family Meeting is a moderated, values-first conversation that aligns generations while everyone is at the table. We turn assumptions into shared understanding and document who does what, when, and why.

#### Transfer more than wealth. Transfer wisdom.

**You’ll leave with:** 

● A shared statement of family values and priorities 

● Clear roles, decisions, and next steps 

● Fewer surprises—and fewer points of conflict—later on 

[LEARN MORE](/family-meeting)

## Discover Your Financial Values

#### Pinpoint the principles that shape your money decisions—and learn how to pass them on.

● 12 quick questions; instant summary on-screen 

● Personalized “values profile” emailed to you (with conversation prompts)

● Perfect primer for a Family Meeting 

[Take the Financial Values Quiz](/financial-reflection)

_We’ll email your results and occasional insights. You can unsubscribe anytime._

## How We Invest

![People sitting around a table engaged in a lively discussion in an office with large windows and green plants.](/images/d51a7dfe8f-RedBarn-Difference1.webp)

#### A portfolio built like a pension—on purpose.

We design around real-life liabilities (education, retirement income, giving) and combine public markets with select institutional-style strategies—private credit, private equity, and real assets—implemented through structures appropriate for family portfolios. The aim: steadier compounding, better downside protection, and alignment with multi-decade goals.

[LEARN MORE](/pension-strategy)

#### Three pillars you can count on:

1.  Disciplined diversification across public markets and select private/real assets for stability and compounding.
    
2.  Risk management tuned to your horizon and cash-flow needs.
    
3.  Discretionary execution so your plan keeps moving—without you chasing markets.
    

### Your first 90 days

-   Discover
    
    We align around your goals, values, obligations, and current holdings.
    
-   Design
    
    We then move into the phase where we create the customized portfolio, tax-aware plan.
    
-   Decide & Deploy
    
    Lastly, we will walk you through a discretionary onboarding, provide clear next steps and ensure everything is implemented.
    

### Are you an advisor?

Extend institutional-grade solutions to your clients without losing the personal relationship. Co-service with transparency; scale your offering.

![Two men in a meeting room having a discussion, with a bar chart displayed on a screen behind them.](/images/c5a08db9f4-GettyImages-1887449071-1-2048x900.webp)

## Canadian Productivity

Sep 11

## **Canada’s Productivity Gap: A Headwind for the Canadian Dollar?**

**Canada’s widening productivity gap with the United States could be one reason the Canadian dollar has remained relatively weak.**

**Currencies are influenced by many factors—including interest rates, commodity prices and capital flows—but over the longer term, productivity and economic competitiveness matter. And on that front, Canada has been losing ground.**

**A recent Fraser Institute report found that Canadian GDP per capita trailed the U.S. by approximately $10,766 (Canadian dollars) in 1999. By 2024, the gap had more than doubled to $23,757.**

### **The Productivity Problem**

**Between 1999 and 2025, U.S. labour productivity increased 67.9%, compared with only 26.7% in Canada.  
**

![](/images/caa308cbab-Sept-11---Prod-Chart.webp)

**Prepared and Retrieved September 08, 2026**

[Hurricanes and Travel](/files/92a387673c-Hurricanes-and-Travel.pdf)

[Tough Talk](https://www.aarp.org/money/personal-finance/how-to-ask-parents-about-finances/)

[Estate Clarity](https://fullspectrumleadership.com/the-conversation-that-changes-everything/)

[OAS](/files/a9a31ca70d-OAS.pdf)

**Business investment tells a similar story. In 2007, Canadian businesses invested about 90 cents per worker for every $1 invested in the U.S. By 2024, that had fallen to just 54 cents.**

**Lower investment in technology, equipment and productive capacity can mean slower economic growth, weaker wage gains and less competitive businesses. Over time, those differences can also make a country less attractive to global capital—potentially creating another headwind for its currency.**

### **What Does This Mean for Investors?**

**Canada remains home to many excellent businesses, but the productivity gap reinforces the importance of looking beyond our borders.**

**The U.S. market provides significantly greater exposure to technology, artificial intelligence, automation and other areas attracting substantial investment and driving productivity growth.**

**For Canadian investors, a weaker Canadian dollar can also increase the Canadian-dollar value of U.S. investments—although currencies can move in either direction.**

**The takeaway: Diversification isn't simply about owning more investments. It's about gaining exposure to different economies, currencies, industries and sources of growth.**

**Source: _Wealth Professional Canada_, Steve Randall, September 1, 2026; Fraser Institute, _Squandering the Canadian Century – Part 1_.**

## **Is the AI Bubble Bursting — or Is This a Buying Opportunity?**

**After several years of extraordinary gains in Artificial Intelligence, technology and semiconductor stocks, investors are being reminded of an old lesson: markets don't go straight up forever.**

**Some of the hottest areas of the market have fallen sharply, raising an important question: Is the AI bubble bursting, or is this simply a correction creating a buying opportunity?**

**We think it could be a little of both.**

**AI may transform the economy, but that doesn't mean every AI-related stock is worth any price. We saw something similar during the Internet boom. The technology changed the world, but many technology stocks still suffered enormous losses when expectations became too optimistic.**

**That's why we don't automatically "buy the dip."**

## **Protecting the Compounding Machine**

**Avoiding large losses is an important part of building long-term wealth. If an investment falls 50%, it needs to rise 100% just to get back to even.**

**So when markets weaken, we ask whether we're seeing a temporary setback or a more important change in direction.**

**If a strong company falls while its underlying business remains healthy, the decline may eventually create an attractive buying opportunity. But if expectations were unrealistic and the longer-term trend is deteriorating, simply buying because the stock is cheaper can be dangerous.**

**At Red Barn, we combine company fundamentals and valuations with economic conditions, market trends and risk-management signals.**

**We don't need to predict whether the AI bubble is bursting. We need to recognize when risks are changing, protect capital when appropriate and be ready to invest when opportunities improve.**

**That's part of what we mean when we say Think Further.

**This week, on July 28th,  the the US Federal Reserve announced that it will not change the overnight interest rate.** 

**This is the  interest rate banks charge each other to borrow reserve balances. When people say “the Fed raised rates” or “the Fed cut rates,” they usually mean the Fed changed this target range.**

**It matters because it influences many other short-term rates across the economy, including savings rates, loan rates, floating-rate debt, and eventually longer-term borrowing costs.**

**What the Bond Market May Be Telling Investors**

The bond market does not always get as much attention as the stock market. Stocks tend to dominate the headlines because they are easier to follow and more familiar to many investors.

But if you want to understand where the economy, inflation, and interest rates may be headed, the bond market is worth watching closely.

In many ways, bonds can act like an early warning system. Bond investors are constantly weighing inflation, economic growth, central bank policy, government borrowing, and recession risk. Because of that, bond yields often move before the broader economy fully shows the change.

That does not mean the bond market is always right. No market has a perfect crystal ball. But bond yields can provide useful clues about what investors are expecting next.  

![](/images/8ca37332dc-July-31---Bond-yields.webp)

**What is the chart telling investors about the economy and inflation?**

-   **The chart shows that long-term borrowing costs stayed high throughout the year, with the 30-year Treasury yield remaining near 5%.**
    
-   **The 2-year yield fell through late 2025 and into early 2026, suggesting investors were expecting lower short-term interest rates.**
    
-   **By spring 2026, the 2-year yield began rising again, which suggests investors became less confident that rate cuts would happen quickly.**
    
-   **The 30-year yield also moved higher into mid-2026, which may point to ongoing concern about inflation, government borrowing, or long-term economic uncertainty.**
    
-   **The gap between the 2-year and 30-year yields stayed wide, showing that investors wanted extra compensation for lending money over many years.**
    
-   **The main message for investors: the bond market is not signaling a collapsing economy, but it is still warning that inflation and long-term borrowing costs remain important risks to watch**.
    

  

###  **Its not all about the economy**   

**  
A well-constructed portfolio should not rely only on the economy or public markets as its main source of return.**

**Many pension plans also invest in assets with return drivers that are less directly tied to stock and bond markets. These are often called alternative investments.**

**One example is a music royalty fund.**

**A music royalty fund earns income from royalties generated when songs are streamed on platforms such as Spotify and Apple Music. In simple terms, the return is connected to music usage and royalty payments, rather than only to economic growth, interest rates, or stock market performance.**

**This does not mean alternative investments are risk-free. They can be less liquid, harder to value, and may not be suitable for every investor. But used thoughtfully, they can add another source of potential return and diversification within a broader portfolio.**

## **Oil Inventory  
**

#### **What this chart may mean for investors**

This chart shows that **U.S. oil inventories (including the Strategic Petroleum Reserve) are near their lowest level in over 45 years**. Think of it as the country having a much smaller "oil savings account" than normal.

**Why it matters:**

-   **Less supply available:** If demand rises or there is a supply disruption (war, hurricane, pipeline outage), there is less oil in storage to make up the difference.
    
-   **Oil prices could rise faster:** Lower inventories often make oil prices more sensitive to unexpected events because there is less of a cushion.
    
-   **Higher inflation risk:** More expensive oil increases the cost of gasoline, transportation and many everyday goods.
    
-   **Interest rates could stay higher:** If higher energy prices push inflation up, central banks may be slower to cut interest rates.
    
-   **Stock market impact:** Higher oil prices are generally positive for energy companies but can be a headwind for the broader stock market because higher fuel costs reduce consumer spending and increase business expenses.
    

**Bottom line:**  
Low oil inventories **do not guarantee** oil prices will rise, but they increase the chances that prices could spike if an unexpected supply problem occurs. That can create both opportunities in the energy sector and increased volatility across the overall stock market.

#### **  
Tokenization**

**  
What is it?  
Tokenization means turning ownership of a real investment, such as a fund, bond, or other asset, into a digital record on a blockchain. You still own the investment, but the record of ownership can be moved, tracked, or settled more efficiently. In simple terms, it is a new way of recording and transferring investments using digital financial infrastructure.  
When  
For most everyday investors, tokenization probably will not change much right away. Over the next several years, it may gradually make some investments faster to buy, sell, transfer, or use inside financial platforms. The bigger impact is likely long term, as more of the financial system adopts digital infrastructure behind the scenes.  
  
To Summarize  
**

-   **Tokenization means representing ownership of an asset on a blockchain, such as a fund, bond, Treasury bill, or other investment.**
    
-   **The key question is whether tokenization improves the investor experience, not simply whether an asset can be put on a blockchain.**
    
-   **Potential benefits include faster settlement, same-day liquidity, easier collateral movement, better transparency, and lower administrative friction.**
    
-   **ETFs offer a useful comparison: they became popular because they made investing simpler, more liquid, more transparent, and more flexible over time.**
    
-   **Tokenization may follow a similar path, moving from a niche idea to a more common investment structure if it proves useful.**
    
-   **Adoption still faces challenges, including limited product availability, uneven investor demand, and fragmented liquidity.**
    
-   **Liquidity is the biggest hurdle, because blockchain can make transactions faster, but it cannot create buyers and sellers on its own.**
    
-   **Stablecoins and tokenized yield products are already gaining traction, especially in payments, settlement, and Treasury-style investments.**
    
-   **Tokenized private credit and other debt products are emerging, but they are still early and need more infrastructure, oversight, and investor confidence.**
    
-   **Bottom line: tokenization is less about a new investment “wrapper” and more about new financial rails that could make markets faster, more transparent, and more efficient over time.**

The above summary was prepared from an article authored by Patrik Björklund, CFA, Innovation Strategist,** [**Janus Henderson**](https://www.janushenderson.com/en-us/advisor/article/tokenisation-why-blockchain-rails-could-redefine-the-future-of-finance/) **on July 20, 2026**

## Commodities

**Canada is rich in natural resources, and the TSX is often influenced by commodity prices. Two of the biggest drivers are oil and gold.**

**When oil and gold rise, it can support parts of the Canadian market, especially energy and materials companies. When they fall, those same sectors can come under pressure.**

**Oil Rises as Gulf Tensions Escalate**

**Iran struck U.S. and Kuwaiti military-linked facilities overnight with missiles and drones. U.S. and coalition defences intercepted many of them, but Kuwait’s main airport was still damaged, with casualties reported.**

**The U.S. responded with strikes on Qeshm Island and also disabled a tanker in the Gulf that it said did not comply with warnings.**

**President Trump says talks with Iran are still ongoing. Iranian media says no talks have taken place. Either way, the fighting is real, and markets are paying attention.**

![](/images/493ee8d07f-June-5.webp)

_Source - TradingView Charting Library  retrieved June 2, 2026_

**Oil moved higher overnight, with Brent up about 2.5% and WTI up about 2.6%. In our model, this moved oil into a bullish trend.**

**Shipping costs are also rising. Maersk has said disruption around the Strait of Hormuz is adding roughly $500 million a month in extra costs.**

**The key takeaway: oil may not be fully pricing in the risk yet. If the conflict continues to disrupt shipping, energy prices and inflation expectations could face more pressure.**

**Source: Associated Press, retrieved June 3, 2026.**

**Gold continues to play an important role in global reserves. Recently, gold overtook U.S. Treasuries as the largest reserve asset held by central banks as indicated by the chart below sourced from the US Department of Treasury. **For investors, this matters because gold is often viewed as a hedge during periods of geopolitical stress, inflation concern, or declining confidence in paper currencies.

**Transportation, production, and input costs often rise alongside oil, which can then influence the price of other commodities over time, including base metals, food, and grains.**

**That does not mean every commodity will rise in lockstep, but it does mean investors should pay attention to how energy shocks can ripple through the cost of living.**

**Why Diversification May Matter More Now**

This article is a short summary of market commentary from David Elms, Head of Diversified Alternatives and Portfolio Manager at Janus Henderson.

For many years, investors benefited from a market backdrop that generally rewarded risk-taking. In that environment, diversification often felt less urgent.

Today, the picture is more complex. Inflation remains uncertain, interest rates are higher than they were through much of the previous cycle, and geopolitical pressures continue to influence markets. As a result, the relationships investors have traditionally relied on, including the balance between stocks and bonds, may be less consistent than in the past.

David Elms’ main point is that diversified alternatives may help complement traditional portfolios in this kind of environment. They are not intended to replace stocks or bonds, but to add other sources of return that may be less tied to broad market direction.

The goal is not to remove risk. It is to build a portfolio that may be more balanced and resilient across a wider range of market conditions.

**5 Takeaways**

1.  Diversification can become more valuable when markets are less predictable.
    
2.  Inflation, higher rates, and geopolitical risk are shaping today’s market environment.
    
3.  The traditional stock-and-bond relationship may be less dependable than before.
    
4.  Diversified alternatives may complement traditional holdings by adding different return drivers.
    
5.  The focus is not on avoiding risk entirely, but on building a more resilient portfolio.

Polymarket is an online prediction market where people use cryptocurrency to bet on the outcome of future events, such as elections, interest rates, sports, or economic news. Prices move based on what traders believe is most likely to happen, making the market a real-time measure of public expectations. Users can profit if they correctly predict outcomes before events are finalized. Built on blockchain technology, Polymarket is designed to be transparent, low cost, and accessible to global investors.

At Red Barn Investment Counsel, we are committed to addressing client concerns fairly and promptly.

What happens next? We will acknowledge receipt of your complaint within 5 business days. 

We will review your complaint promptly and aim to provide a substantive response within 90 days. If we need more time, we will let you know. ## Clarity over guesswork.

#### Discretionary management turns your plan into a living mandate. We agree on guardrails, then execute with discipline—so rebalancing, risk management, and tax-aware adjustments happen on time, not on impulse.

PENSION STRATEGY //

## Add resilience. Broaden what drives returns.

#### Traditional 60/40 can be fragile in certain regimes. Institutions diversify _drivers_ of return by adding strategies like private credit, private equity, and real assets. We adapt that approach thoughtfully for family portfolios—sized to your liquidity and time horizon.

**_While we draw on principles used by institutional pension funds, this is not a pension and does not provide guaranteed income. Investment returns will vary and capital is at risk. Past performance is not indicative of future results._**

-   **Different engines:** returns not solely tied to public equities
    
-   **Potentially smoother ride:** lower correlation across economic cycles
    
-   **Design for life:** align to future liabilities (education, retirement income, giving)
    

-   How we size & structure
    
    -   Suitability first; right-size by liquidity & risk

    -   Long-horizon families open to a measured alt sleeve
        
    -   Investors wanting resilience without complexity sprawl

    -   Investors wanting resilience to market volatility

[START WITH AN INTRO CALL](/start-here)

OUR STORY //

## Built for the long view

![An older man and woman standing and talking outdoors during sunset with mountain scenery in the background.](/images/40ef197517-image-gen--3-.webp)

We started Red Barn to bring institutional discipline to family portfolios—and to make space for something bigger than returns alone: stewardship. The work is practical and human. It’s about providing for today, preserving capacity to sow again, and making room for legacy.

[MEET THE TEAM](/our-team)

[ADVISOR RELATIONSHIPS](/advisor-relationships)

DISCRETIONARY MANAGEMENT //

## Why “Red Barn”

#### Across the countryside, red barns safeguard the harvest—ensuring families have abundance through the winter and seed to plant in spring. That picture guides our decisions. Portfolios should protect what’s been earned, sustain what’s needed, and keep the next season in view. For us, investing is a means to continuity: values carried forward, opportunities funded on purpose, and fewer surprises for the people you love.

![A group of four people, including a teenage girl, an elderly woman, and two adult men, smiling outdoors in front of trees with yellow and green leaves.](/images/d18b0a4d3b-logan-weaver-lgnwvr-5k-vpipIa7w-unsplash.webp)

### Three principles we operate by

-   **Provide for today:** design cash flows and guardrails you can live with.
    
-   **Preserve capacity to sow again:** keep a growth engine working behind the scenes.
    
-   **Make room for legacy:** align structures and roles so wisdom—not just wealth—passes on.
    

WHO WE ARE //

## Our Values

#### (and what they look like in practice)

![A grandfather, a young woman, and a small boy are sitting on a wooden bench outdoors, smiling and laughing together amidst a fall setting with trees showing autumn colors.](/images/51a9412928-image-gen--4-.webp)

-   We treat every decision as if a future generation will read the notes.
    
-   _In practice:_ documented mandates, rules-based rebalancing, quarterly reviews.
    

#### Stewardship

-   Plain English, no mystery.
    
-   _In practice:_ simple diagrams, clear reporting, “why” behind each change.
    

#### Clarity

-   Process over headlines.
    
-   _In practice:_ risk guardrails, rebalancing triggers, tax-aware implementation.
    

#### Discipline

-   Advice first, products second.
    
-   _In practice:_ third-party custody, transparent fees, no sales agenda.
    

#### Independence

-   Wealth is a tool for good.
    
-   _In practice:_ Family Meeting facilitation, giving strategies, “giving while alive.”
    

#### Generosity

-   Compounding needs time and calm.
    
-   _In practice:_ horizon-based portfolios and behaviour coaching through cycles.
    

#### Patience

![Logo of Red Barn Investment Counsel with a stylized barn illustration above the text.](/images/b27dc70ad2-RedBarn-Logo.webp)

**_We charge a transparent advisory fee based on assets under management. We do not receive commissions or trailer fees from product manufacturers._**

![A multi-generational family sitting on a porch, smiling and laughing together, with autumn trees in the background.](/images/f12b90f6eb-image-gen--1-.webp)

_Discretionary • Fiduciary-minded • Third-party custody • Transparent fees_

A guided, values-first session that aligns generations on roles, decisions, and next steps.

[EXPLORE THE FAMILY MEETING](/family-meeting)

#### Advisor Relationships

For insurance brokers, wealth advisors, and planners who want a fiduciary standard to execute under a co-branded mandate.

[ADVISOR RELATIONSHIPS](/advisor-relationships)

## Our Team

Behind every portfolio is a partnership. Get to know the advisors and operators who align your plan to what matters now and what endures.

![Group portrait of four professionally dressed individuals standing indoors, smiling at the camera.](/images/2d8b4fb1fe-20251112-RedBarn-8709-FIN.v2.webp)

## Meet the team

![An elderly man dressed in a dark blue plaid suit with a red tie stands beside a wooden table in a modern office setting, smiling at the camera.](/images/b9d2b61eb1-20251112-RedBarn-8655-FIN.webp)

#### CFA, Founder and Portfolio Manager

[Greg Flower](mailto:gflower@REDBARNINVESTMENTCOUNSEL.CA?subject=From%20Website)

Greg brings a depth of experience and a disciplined investment mindset to Red Barn Investment Counsel, grounded in capital preservation, thoughtful risk management, and sustainable long-term growth. His education, professional training, and decades of hands-on experience form the foundation of a pragmatic and client-focused investment approach.

-   Expand Bio
    
    Greg earned his Bachelor of Commerce from the University of Calgary and became a Chartered Accountant in 1982. He went on to co-found Peterson and Flower Chartered Accountants, successfully operating the firm from 1983 to 1988. From 1988 to 1993, Greg served as Assistant Auditor General of Bermuda, gaining valuable international experience in public finance, governance, and accountability.  
    
    While in Bermuda, Greg earned the Chartered Financial Analyst designation in 1992. Returning to Canada, he began building his financial services practice, working as an Investment Advisor from 1993 to 2000. In 2001, he achieved a long-standing professional goal by becoming a Portfolio Manager, allowing him to directly apply his investment philosophy on behalf of clients. His ultimate goal, the founding of Red Barn Investment Counsel was achieved in 2019.
    
    Born and raised in Calgary, Greg and his wife Catherine raised their three sons there and remain deeply connected to the community. They are also proud grandparents of four. Outside the office, Greg enjoys staying active through mountain biking, golf, and skiing—activities that reflect the balance, discipline, and long-term perspective he brings to his work as a portfolio manager.
    

![An older man with glasses and a balding head, smiling, wearing a patterned blue blazer, light orange shirt, and a pocket square, standing indoors with a neutral background.](/images/a09570f2b8--O9A0784-Edit.webp)

#### Financial Life Planner

[Bryce Medd](mailto:bmedd@REDBARNINVESTMENTCOUNSEL.CA?subject=From%20Website)

Through a strategic alliance, Red Barn Investment Counsel has engaged the expertise and wisdom of Wealthy Tortoise Financial Group Inc., and Bryce Medd, as a financial life planner and risk management specialist.

-   Expand Bio
    
    Bryce is a charter holder of the Registered Financial Planner (R.F.P.) and Trust and Estate Practitioner (TEP) designations.
    
    With a “seek first to understand” approach to business and life, Bryce adds invaluable experience and expertise through questioning, hence his CQO title – Chief Questioning Officer
    

![A man in a black suit, white shirt, and maroon tie smiling in an office setting, with a potted plant to his left and modern artwork on the wall behind him.](/images/cb6624af36-20251112-RedBarn-8628-FIN.webp)

#### Private Client Wealth Manager 

[Francis Bustamante](mailto:fbustamante@REDBARNINVESTMENTCOUNSEL.CA?subject=From%20Website) 

My approach to wealth management is built on a simple belief: a portfolio is only as strong as the life plan it supports. With a background as a financial advisor and a deep commitment to client-centric service, I am currently pursuing the Chartered Investment Manager (CIM) designation to elevate further the expertise I bring to the families I serve.

-   Expand Bio
    
    Bridging Goals and Strategy At Red Barn Investment Counsel, I act as the vital link between a family's aspirations and their investment strategy. I spend the core of my time helping clients define their most meaningful life goals—whether that involves multi-generational legacy planning or reaching major personal milestones. By translating these objectives into actionable insights for our investment team, I ensure that every portfolio is genuinely tailored to your life.  
    After immigrating to Canada with my parents in the early nineties, I moved to Calgary after a brief stint in Toronto; my commitment to my Community is deeply personal. I serve as the Chairman of the Board for Supreme Hoops Canada, a non-profit dedicated to youth, and I am a passionate advocate for Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) research. Since my son's diagnosis, fundraising to find a cure has become a lifelong mission. This work mirrors my professional life: providing hope and a clear path forward for families navigating complex challenges.  
    I'm a firm believer that a balanced life is a successful one. To stay energized, I set aside time for weight training and playing basketball. When I'm not at the gym or in the boardroom, you'll likely find me in the kitchen experimenting with new recipes or at a local venue enjoying live music. Whether I'm in the kitchen or crafting a financial plan, I've learned that the best results come from the right ingredients, careful preparation, and a genuine passion for the craft.
    

![A woman with long brown hair and blue eyes smiling, standing with arms crossed in a modern office with a plant and abstract artwork in the background.](/images/343bec4311-20251112-RedBarn-8691-FIN.webp)

#### Client Operations Coordinator

[Klara Crowley](mailto:Kcrowley@redbarninvestmentcounsel.ca?subject=From%20Website)

My approach to operations is grounded in a simple principle: efficiency is the backbone of exceptional client service. With a bachelor's degree in business management from Western University and a passion for creating structure in dynamic environments, I focus on building systems that keep everything running seamlessly behind the scenes. Attention to detail and organizational excellence aren’t just skills, they’re the tools I use to ensure our team can deliver on its promises every single day.

-   Expand Bio
    
    As Operations Manager at Red Barn, I help facilitate the link between vision and execution. My role is to translate strategic goals into actionable processes that support both our advisors and our clients. Whether it’s streamlining workflows or implementing new solutions, I thrive on the challenge of making complex operations simple and effective.  
    I was born and raised in the Okanagan and made the exciting move to Calgary in September 2024. This transition has been an opportunity to grow personally and professionally while embracing a vibrant new community. Outside of work, my friends and family are what bring me the most joy and I spend most of my free time with them. Whether it’s sharing a meal, exploring the outdoors, or simply enjoying quality time together, you'll usually catch me with a smile on my face.

## Privacy Policy

**Vesta and Your Privacy**

Vesta Wealth Partners Ltd. considers your personal privacy to be an important part of our service to you. We understand the need to safeguard information about you that you have entrusted to us. As part of our commitment to you we have adopted principles designed to protect your privacy and prevent misuse of your personal information and help you understand our commitment to your personal privacy.

References to " Vesta ", "we" or"our" are to Vesta Wealth Partners Ltd.. Where we use the term"personal information" we are referring to any information that identifies you as an individual and includes information with respect to your name, address, age, gender, income, marital status, finances, employment, trading history and Website use information, together with your personal references and identification numbers (such as a social insurance number).

Our privacy policy applies to personal clients, including individuals carrying on business alone or in partnership with other individuals. The following sections will answer most of the important questions that you may have about how we gather, protect and use personal information, and how we will hold ourselves accessible and accountable to you.

**Vesta 's Principles on Privacy**

We have incorporated certain principles for the protection of personal information in our privacy policy.

-   Collecting and Using Personal Information - We will explain how we intend to use your personal information prior to or when we are collecting it and we will limit the personal information we collect to what we need for those purposes. We will use it only for those purposes we have explained to you and we will obtain your consent if we wish to use your personal information for any other purpose.
    
-   Disclosing Personal Information to Others - We may provide your personal information to other persons not affiliated with Vesta, such as regulators, service providers or credit reporting agencies, but only where we have your consent or where we are required or permitted to do so by law.
    
-   Retaining and Protecting Personal Information - We will retain your personal information only for the time it is required for the purposes we explain or as otherwise required by law. We will protect the personal information we obtain about you with appropriate safeguards and security measures.
    
-   Access and Accuracy - We will provide you with reasonable access to your personal information on record with Vesta and information about Vesta 's use and disclosure of that information. We will make every reasonable effort to keep your personal information accurate and up-to-date.
    
-   Accountability and Openness to Your Privacy Concerns - We will hold ourselves accountable to you and we will investigate and respond to your concerns about any aspect of our handling of your personal information. We will explain the application of our privacy policy to your personal information and explain your options of refusing or withdrawing consent to the collection, use and release of your personal information, and we will record and respect your choices.
    

**Why Does Vesta Collect Personal Information?**

We collect, retain, and use personal information about you only when we reasonably believe that it will help administer our business or provide products, services and other opportunities to you as our client. We collect and retain personal information about you only for specific business purposes - and we will tell you why we are collecting and retaining it on your request. The information we ask for depends on the products or services you request and in most cases are required by law or the policies of the regulatory bodies to which we are subject.

Your social insurance number is required for products that earn investment income, in order to comply with the Canada Revenue Agency's income reporting requirements. If you provide your social insurance number, we also use it to keep your personal information separate from that of other clients with a similar name.

With your consent, we may share your personal information, where not prohibited by law, to affiliated companies of Vesta for the purposes of providing other services to you. Vesta may use your personal information to provide you with information about Vesta's products and services and other matters. This consent is optional and you can decide to withdraw it at anytime. Please refer to our section regarding your options below.

**How Does Vesta Collect Personal Information?**

We obtain most of our information about you directly from you. With your consent, we may obtain personal information about you from third parties.

**When Does Vesta Release Personal Information?**

Vesta does not sell client lists or personal information to others.

We do not reveal personal information about you to parties outside our affiliated companies for their independent use unless you request or authorize it or the information is provided in order to complete a transaction initiated by you or the disclosure otherwise is lawfully permitted or required. We may disclose information to the authorities to serve a clear public interest and fulfill our public duty - such as to protect against fraud, money laundering or other criminal activity. We may, from time to time, be requested to disclose information to regulators to which we are subject for the purposes of an audit or investigation relating to specific accounts or our business generally. In certain circumstances, Vesta may disclose your personally identifiable information if it believes, in good faith, that disclosure is otherwise necessary or advisable to protect its interests.

Sometimes it is necessary to provide personal information about you to a party outside our company, such as to a vendor or service company that we hire to do our data processing or prepare your account statements or to provide support or services for one or more of our products. These vendors and service companies agree to safeguard confidential information about you and your products and services with us and must abide by applicable law.

**Does Vesta provide options?**

It is always your choice whether or not to provide personal information or to consent to our obtaining personal information about you from third parties. In many cases you are free to refuse or withdraw your consent at any time. If you choose not to provide requested personal information or consents, we may not be able to provide certain products and services to you or you may be ineligible for or be unable to use certain products and services we provide.

Vesta will explain your options of refusing or withdrawing consent to the collection, use or release of your personal information, and we will record and respect your choices. If you wish to discuss your options you may do so by contacting Vesta's designated privacy officer set out below, or contacting our Compliance Department. Our staff will be pleased to explain your options and any consequences of refusing or withdrawing your consent.

**How Long Does Vesta Retain Personal Information?**

We retain your personal information only as long as it is required for the reasons it was collected or as required by law.
